challengeTypes: identify: What is a PowerPoint TEMPLATE? (A pre-designed layout for slides vs A type of font | A type of animation | A type of transition)

sort: Drag each PowerPoint feature to its correct description (Template = pre-designed slide layout | Theme = coordinated colors, fonts, and effects | Color scheme = set of matching colors | Chart = visual data representation | Slide sorter = view to rearrange slides | Objects = text boxes, shapes, images on slides)
identify: Which view lets you see and rearrange ALL slides as thumbnails? (Slide Sorter view vs Slide Show view vs Reading view vs Outline view)

sort: Drag each programming concept to its correct description (Algorithm = step-by-step instructions to solve a problem | Program = algorithm written in a programming language | Code = the actual instructions in a programming language | Algorithm = like a recipe | Program = like the cooked dish | Programming = writing code from algorithm)
identify: What is the Scratch STAGE? (The area where sprites perform and show actions vs The area where you write code | The area where you choose blocks | The area where you save files)

sort: Drag each Scratch interface part to its correct description (Stage = area where sprites perform | Sprite = a character or object that acts | Blocks palette = collection of coding blocks | Scripts area = where you drag and stack blocks | Paint editor = tool to draw or edit sprites | Costumes = different looks for a sprite)
identify: Which block category in Scratch is used to START a script? (Event blocks vs Motion blocks vs Looks blocks vs Sound blocks)

sort: Drag each block type to its correct category (When flag clicked = Event | Move 10 steps = Motion | Say Hello = Looks | Play sound meow = Sound | When key pressed = Event | Change color = Looks | Glide to x y = Motion | Set size = Looks)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) PowerPoint templates, themes, color schemes — Template: a pre-designed slide layout with placeholders for text, images, and content. Theme: a coordinated set of colors, fonts, and effects applied to all slides. Color scheme: a set of matching colors that complement each other. Using templates and themes makes presentations look professional and consistent. (2) PowerPoint objects, charts, slide sorter — Objects: text boxes, shapes, images, and charts placed on slides. Charts: visual representations of data (bar chart, pie chart, line chart). Slide sorter view: shows all slides as thumbnails, allows rearranging, deleting, and duplicating slides. (3) Concept of program and programming — Algorithm: a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem (like a recipe). Program: an algorithm written in a programming language that a computer can execute. Programming: the process of writing code from an algorithm. Algorithm comes first, then code. (4) Scratch interface — Stage: the area where sprites perform and show their actions. Sprite: a character or object that acts on the stage (the Scratch cat is the default sprite). Blocks palette: a collection of colored coding blocks organized by category. Scripts area: where you drag and stack blocks to create scripts. Paint editor: tool to draw or edit sprites and costumes. Costumes: different looks/appearances for a sprite. (5) Creating and moving sprites — Use the paint editor to draw new sprites or edit existing ones. Save sprites to the sprite library. Move sprites using motion blocks. (6) Scratch scripts — Event blocks: start scripts (when flag clicked, when key pressed). Motion blocks: move sprites (move 10 steps, glide to x y, turn degrees). Looks blocks: change appearance (say Hello, change color, set size). Sound blocks: play sounds (play sound meow). Misconceptions: 'a template and a theme are the same' (WRONG — a template is a slide LAYOUT; a theme is coordinated COLORS, FONTS, and EFFECTS), 'an algorithm and a program are the same' (WRONG — an algorithm is step-by-step instructions in plain language; a program is those instructions written in a programming language), 'the stage and the scripts area are the same' (WRONG — the stage is where sprites PERFORM; the scripts area is where you WRITE the code), 'event blocks are not important' (WRONG — event blocks are essential because they START the script; without an event block, the script will not run), 'Scratch is only for making games' (WRONG — Scratch can make stories, animations, music, and interactive presentations, not just games).
